title: U.S. House · Hawaii's 2nd District
area: Rural Oahu and the neighbor islands of Hawaii (the Big Island), Maui, Kauai, and Molokai.

context.text: Incumbent Jill Tokuda (D) won the August 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 91.6% of the vote. Brenton Awa, a Hawaii state senator, ran unopposed for the Republican nomination. Edward Codelia won the nonpartisan primary with 62.5% of the vote over Randall Terry.

candidates.name: Jill Tokuda

summary.text: Jill Tokuda is the Democratic incumbent for Hawaii's 2nd District, first elected in 2022. A Honolulu native, she served in the Hawaii Senate from 2006 to 2018, including as Ways and Means chair, and worked in nonprofit and private-sector roles before Congress. She is running for re-election on her record in Congress.

background.text: Born in Honolulu in 1976. According to her official biography, her family has lived in the district for four generations since emigrating from Okinawa, and she attended Hawaii public schools.
Earned a B.A. in international relations from George Washington University in 1997; her official biography adds a minor in Japanese studies and says she was the first in her family to attend college.

Worked as president of Kalliope LLC and co-director of CyberHawaii, a workforce development organization, and as external affairs director of the Nisei Veterans Memorial Center, where she raised funds to expand the facility on Maui.

Served in the Hawaii State Senate from 2006 to 2018, representing Kaneohe and Kailua. She chaired the Ways and Means, Education and Higher Education, Agriculture and Hawaiian Affairs, and Labor committees.

As Ways and Means chair, her office says she approved all fiscal and tax measures and championed legislation creating the state's Executive Office on Early Learning and the Hawai'i Keiki Program, and enabling legislation for Important Agricultural Lands.

Won the 2022 Democratic primary with 57.6 percent in an open-seat race and the November 2022 general election with 62.2 percent, taking office January 3, 2023. She was re-elected in 2024 with 66.5 percent.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and is ranking member of the Agriculture Subcommittee on Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology. She is co-chair of the Bipartisan Rural Health Caucus and second vice chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus.

Served on the Hawaii House Select Committee on COVID-19 Economic and Financial Preparedness during the pandemic and was a founding member of the Patsy T. Mink PAC. Her official biography says she is married to Kyle Michibata and they have two sons.
Won the August 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 91.6 percent of the vote.

priorities.text: Protecting Hawai'i's military training lands from federal condemnation, saying any future use of the lands must be built on good-faith negotiation with the local community.
Strengthening rural hospitals' access to Medicare and Medicaid funding so they can keep their doors open and maintain critical services.
Advocates for "commonsense gun safety laws" that she says protect communities while respecting individual rights.

positions.summary: After the Supreme Court struck down a Hawai'i law requiring concealed-carry permit holders to get permission before bringing firearms onto private property open to the public, said she would keep fighting for stricter gun safety laws.
positions.quote: I will keep fighting for commonsense gun safety laws that protect our people, respect everyone’s rights, and prioritizes our communities' ability to determine what safety looks like for ourselves.

positions.summary: Joined 26 House colleagues in a joint statement opposing a proposed $3.3 billion in additional Foreign Military Financing to Israel, citing civilian deaths in Gaza and Lebanon and unenforced human-rights conditions on U.S. security assistance.
positions.quote: For this reason, we do not support providing an additional $3.3 billion of American taxpayer dollars to be used for Israeli military operations in Gaza and Lebanon—operations which have killed tens of thousands of civilians, led to the indiscriminate destruction of civilian infrastructure, and caused severe and ongoing humanitarian catastrophes.

positions.summary: Applauded the Supreme Court's decision striking down the Trump administration's IEEPA tariffs and introduced a bill to eliminate tariffs on imported farm inputs, saying broad tariffs have raised costs for farmers and families.
positions.quote: No president should be able to unilaterally gamble with our economy, effectively taxing American families, farmers, and small businesses.

record.text: Serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the House Armed Services Committee (Military Personnel and Readiness Subcommittees) in the 118th Congress committee assignments listed on Ballotpedia.

Introduced the bipartisan Rural Emergency Hospital Designation Improvement Act (REH 2.0) to expand which rural hospitals can qualify for the Rural Emergency Hospital designation and its Medicare payments.

As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, helped advance the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act (H.R. 8800) and blocked a provision that would have authorized unilateral Army condemnation of military training lands in Hawai'i, voting for the bill's passage out of committee.

candidates.name: Brenton Awa

summary.text: Brenton Awa is the Republican nominee and a Hawaii state senator for District 23 (Windward and North Shore Oahu), first elected in 2022 and Senate minority leader. A former television journalist, he has said he would serve only one term in Congress. His campaign says it is focused on housing affordability and restoring Hawaii's federal influence.

background.text: Born in Ka'a'awa, Oahu, on February 19, 1986, and raised in Kahalu'u; graduated from Kahuku High School in 2004.
Earned a degree in speech communication and leadership from Clarion University of Pennsylvania (now Pennsylvania Western University - Clarion), where he wrestled, according to Wikipedia.

Began his television news career in 2009 at KGMB in Honolulu and joined KITV as a reporter in 2015, later serving as morning and evening anchor, according to Wikipedia. Hawaii News Now describes him as a former television journalist.
Won election to the Hawaii State Senate in November 2022, defeating incumbent Democrat Gil Riviere 51.3 to 48.7 percent, and was re-elected in 2024 over Ben Shafer, 52.7 to 47.3 percent.
Serves as Senate minority leader, a post he has held since 2024, and sits on the Agriculture and Environment, Commerce and Consumer Protection, and Judiciary committees (2025-2026).

According to his campaign website, his Senate work includes intervening in a state plan to raise rents for Waiahole farmers, creating roadside food forests in Kahalu'u and Hale'iwa, and passing a bill through the Senate to ban foreign ownership of agricultural land.
Announced his run for Congress in October 2025 while keeping his Senate seat, whose term runs to 2028, and ran unopposed in the August 8, 2026 Republican primary.

positions.summary: Voted no on SB 401, which banned the sale, manufacture, and possession of assault pistols and certain other semi-automatic firearms.
Voted no on SB 3202, which allowed up to two accessory dwelling units on residential lots statewide.

record.text: Serves on the Hawaii State Senate's Agriculture and Environment, Commerce and Consumer Protection, and Judiciary committees (2025-2026 term).
Voted no on SB 401 (banning the sale, manufacture, and possession of assault pistols and other rifles/shotguns meeting statutory criteria), which passed the Hawai'i Senate 20-5 on March 4, 2025.
Voted no on SB 3202 (allowing up to two accessory dwelling units on residential lots statewide), which passed the Hawai'i Senate 16-9 on May 1, 2024.

Voted no on SB 1396 (raising the transient accommodations tax and applying it to cruise ships to fund climate and environmental programs, the "Green Fee"), which passed the Hawai'i Senate 23-2 on May 2, 2025.

candidates.researchNotes: Awa has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for this race and his campaign website could not be reached within the research window, so his stated priorities and issue positions could not be independently verified beyond his state legislative committee record.

candidates.name: Edward Codelia

summary.text: Edward Codelia is a nonpartisan candidate for Hawaii's 2nd District who works as a real estate professional. He received 62.5 percent of the vote in the August 2026 nonpartisan primary. He says he is running on independent representation, accountability, disaster preparedness, and affordability.

background.text: Career experience includes working as a real estate professional, according to Ballotpedia. No education or prior offices are listed.
Says his first jobs were shoveling snow, raking leaves, mowing lawns, and delivering newspapers in his neighborhood.
Received 1,230 votes (62.5 percent) to Randall Terry's 738 in the August 8, 2026 nonpartisan primary; Ballotpedia records that no nonpartisan candidate advanced from that primary.

priorities.text: Independent representation focused on accountability rather than party politics.
Protecting Hawaii's natural environment and cultural heritage in federal decisions.
Making Hawaii more affordable by addressing housing, food, energy, transportation, and healthcare costs specific to island living.
Disaster preparedness and infrastructure investment, citing the Maui wildfires as showing the need for better planning and emergency communications.

candidates.researchNotes: Codelia has no prior officeholding record; positions are drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
